scope: Gate 2, smallest staging path, the parts provable without touching live infrastructure: verified signed configuration and releases, and the M4 validating sole anchor writer. Nothing here is deployed; the deployed synthetic execution needs the approvals listed below.

verified_signed_configuration.change: The served process takes its profile only from signed releases: the trust inventory is verified against the pinned release root, then the active profile, the privacy policy it names and the partition's spending grant are verified to their exact bytes and resolved as one set (VerifiedProfileAuthority over load_authorized_profile). Route, rates, bounds, deadline and policy all come from verified content; nothing is local.

verified_signed_configuration.method: Each case mints its own release root and release key, signs a real inventory and real profile, policy and grant releases, and installs them through the authority store's ordinary verify, stage and activate path as the release manager.
verified_signed_configuration.defect_found: The release manager, holding exactly its deployed grants, could not activate a spending grant: the role template granted nothing on grant_releases or spending_partitions, and the authority store never set tiamat.partition_id, which both tables' row-level security requires. The only earlier grant-activation test ran as the database owner. Fixed: the store scopes the partition for grant writes, and the template and the disposable fixture grant the narrowest rights grant staging and projection need. The first fix let grant activation clear any partition block; it now clears only no_active_grant, so an unfunded settlement liability outlives a new grant.

It now refuses quarantined -> continuity_established (recovery_continuity_requires_pending) and requires recovery_pending -> continuity_established to carry the pending witness unchanged. It applies to every adapter, not only the writer.

infrastructure_as_code.tiamat-recovery-anchor-v1.yaml: the coordinator's PutItem is removed (it keeps GetItem), and the table's own resource policy denies PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, BatchWriteItem and PartiQL writes to every principal but the writer role
infrastructure_as_code.tiamat-anchor-writer-v1.yaml: writer role (identity grant LeadingKeys-scoped; trust pinned to its own function), function with reserved concurrency 1 from a pinned artifact version and code digest, invoke permission granted to the coordinator role, and a CloudTrail trail delivered to CloudWatch Logs recording item writes on the table and all management writes. Metric filters raise ForeignAnchorWrites (item write by any other role session or any non-role identity) and AnchorBoundaryChanges (the table's policy, protection or existence; the writer function's code, configuration, alias or permissions; the writer role's policies), each alarming to the SNS topic
infrastructure_as_code.invoke_boundary: The coordinator's invoke grant is additive, not exclusive: other same-account principals holding lambda:InvokeFunction can also invoke. That is safe because the writer believes nothing unsigned; the privileged surface is changing the function or its role, which the boundary alarm reports.
infrastructure_as_code.template_tests: structural only: they assert the policies, filters and alarms are present and shaped as intended. Nothing is deployed, cfn-lint has not run, and whether each filter matches real CloudTrail records can only be shown on staging.

m4_anchor_writer.lambda_packaging: The writer's import chain no longer loads psycopg (the continuity beacon reader imports it lazily). It still needs rfc8785, which is not in the hash-locked Lambda dependency list, and the artifact builder packages only lucy.contracts and lucy.executors today.

The foreign-writer alarm goes to an existing SNS topic supplied as a parameter.

found_and_fixed: HIGH: the EventBridge foreign-writer rule could never fire, because DynamoDB item-level data events are not delivered to EventBridge. Replaced by a table resource policy that denies item writes to all but the writer, plus CloudWatch Logs metric filters and alarms, including management events.
MEDIUM: verifying the head at its witness not_before could permanently refuse a genuine head issued late in its key's window. Now verified at the signed issued_at.
MEDIUM: 'invoke only from the coordinator' was overstated. Reworded; writer function and role changes now alarm, and the role's trust is pinned to its function.
MEDIUM: the new release-manager grant made grant activation able to clear an unfunded settlement block. Activation now clears only no_active_grant.
LOW: a read/read race reported record_invalid; it now reports compare_failed.
The missing-head-inventory case is distinguished from a junk head.
confirmed_sound: Historical head verification and reading key id and identity from unverified bytes: closed by the root-signed transition binding the witness digest and the witness binding its inventory digest.
G9 as implemented; pending renewal, quarantined -> pending and established -> pending with a new generation remain allowed.
Principal set to a role ARN is valid for AWS::Lambda::Permission.
Verified configuration: route, rates, bounds, deadline and policy come only from verified content.
not_changed: VerifiedProfileAuthority opens four connections per call, at admission and on every replay-eligibility check. Correct; a connection-count risk to watch on Render rather than a change made now.
The ApiRelease policy header is still local configuration; it is not compared with ledger state.

deployment_package.roots_pinned_into_the_version: WriterRootsSha256 is a stack parameter, an environment variable and part of the Lambda version's description beside the code digest. Either changing replaces the version resource, so a new version is published and the live alias moves to it; the writer refuses to start when its roots do not hash to the published digest.

metric_filters_tested_by_aws.method: CloudWatch Logs TestMetricFilter, which evaluates patterns and changes nothing in the account, run against the template's own patterns rendered as the stack renders them. The events are synthetic records in CloudTrail's shape, with each API's own request fields; whether real denied events carry resources[].ARN for every write API is established only at staging step 5.
metric_filters_tested_by_aws.foreign_writes: match: coordinator PutItem, a coordinator TransactWriteItems whose second resource is the anchor table, a coordinator PartiQL statement, a coordinator BatchWriteItem, an IAM user put, a root delete. No match: the writer's own put, a read, a write to another table.
metric_filters_tested_by_aws.boundary_changes: match: table resource policy removed, table updated, writer configuration, code, alias and published version changed, writer role inline policy, attached managed policy and trust policy changed. No match: the writer's own put, another function, another role.
metric_filters_tested_by_aws.array_selector: The same AWS evaluation with the previous resources[0] pattern misses the transaction whose anchor-table resource is second; resources[*] catches it.
metric_filters_tested_by_aws.test: tests/integration/test_tiamat_anchor_writer_filters_aws.py, run with TIAMAT_AWS_FILTER_TEST=1: 2 passed (13 foreign-or-not and 12 boundary-or-not events)

serving_process.consume_only: A deployed serving process never holds the recovery credential, as the role template requires. start_serving without a launcher consumes a waiting claimant or refuses with startup_claimant_required; proven on the disposable ledger, then served 200 after the separate launcher issued one. A recovery credential placed in the runtime slot is refused at startup (runtime_credential_is_not_the_runtime_role), also proven on the disposable ledger.
serving_process.environment_loader: served_environment.create_app_from_environment (uvicorn factory) builds the process from its environment and committed trust, and refuses a recovery credential, any transport but synthetic, a ledger ID or environment that differs from its independent pin, a release root that differs from its pin, and any missing value; at startup it also refuses unless the runtime URL logs in as the runtime role. 9 unit cases.

deployment_package.open_before_the_deployed_synthetic_reque: The served process dispatches only under an established anchor for its own ledger. The commissioned ledger stays quarantined, and no other ledger has an anchor record. A disposable staging identity needs its own throwaway writer root and signed quarantined -> recovery_pending -> continuity_established transitions; the offline builders today sign only quarantined ones. That tooling is the next local piece.
